theme: time-varying carbon, time-of-use price, charging scheduling, and nonlinear charging
ranking_basis: mechanism fit with current E4/E5 gaps
ability to isolate contribution under the same full-evaluation budget

candidates.name: FIXED_ROUTE_NONLINEAR_CHARGING_LABEL_OPTIMIZER
candidates.mechanism: For a fixed customer sequence, jointly select charging-station insertions, charging times, and partial nonlinear charge amounts using forward/backward time-SOC functions and label dominance.
candidates.difference_from_standard_alns: Adds an optimization oracle over charging decisions after route moves instead of using only station insertion or constant-power feasibility repair.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Restore NL-to-NL feasibility and reduce route duration or formal cost on routes whose linear charging replay is infeasible or direction-reversing.
candidates.complexity: Pseudo-polynomial or label-count dependent; worst case exponential without strong dominance.
candidates.budget_accounting: Each complete solution produced for ALNS acceptance consumes one search evaluation; label expansions and oracle calls are separate diagnostic counters and wall time.
failure_risks: incorrect dominance under time-varying price and carbon
new SOC or time discretization would require approval
candidates.minimum_isolated_probe: Hand-enumerated micro routes plus dense-grid oracle; verify nonlinear duration, SOC, feasibility, station insertion, and objective equality.

candidates.name: RCSP_CHARGING_ORACLE_CSPY
candidates.mechanism: Represent charging opportunities in a directed time-SOC graph and solve a constrained shortest path with custom resource extension functions.
candidates.formal_integration_point_if_approved: subprocess or dependency behind a versioned charging-oracle interface
candidates.difference_from_standard_alns: Supplies an exact or heuristic resource-feasible charging subproblem rather than another destroy-repair weight.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: A lower-friction Python prototype for validating time, SOC, price, carbon, and availability resource semantics.
candidates.complexity: Label-count dependent and potentially exponential; Python graph construction may dominate small-route runtime.
candidates.budget_accounting: Oracle calls, generated labels, dominated labels, runtime, and complete solution evaluations must be logged separately.
failure_risks: repository code is generic and last pushed in 2024
custom nonlinear resource may violate bidirectional assumptions
candidates.minimum_isolated_probe: Budget-free functional probe only; compare with exhaustive enumeration on tiny fixed routes.

candidates.name: RCSP_CHARGING_ORACLE_PATHWYSE
candidates.mechanism: Use PathWyse bidirectional dynamic programming, customizable nonlinear resources, dominance, DSSR/NG-path, and join procedures for a charging RCSP.
candidates.proposed_isolated_location: external isolated process only until license approval
candidates.formal_integration_point_if_approved: to be decided only after GPL review
candidates.difference_from_standard_alns: High-performance extensible labeling engine; it is infrastructure, not by itself a paper innovation.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Outperform the cspy prototype if charging labels become the runtime bottleneck.
candidates.complexity: Label-count dependent; C++ implementation can reduce constant factors.
candidates.budget_accounting: Same accounting as C3-02 with subprocess startup and serialization time included.
failure_risks: performance on generic RCSP may not transfer
candidates.minimum_isolated_probe: Only after explicit license and prototype approval; use the same tiny cases as C3-02.

candidates.name: ROLLING_CARBON_AWARE_CHARGING_SCHEDULER
candidates.mechanism: At each rolling step, optimize active EV charging power over a forecast horizon under arrival/departure, SOC, per-EV power, and site transformer constraints.
candidates.formal_integration_point_if_approved: E4 fixed-route scheduler and E7 rolling charging subproblem
candidates.difference_from_standard_alns: Adds a rolling charging controller and matched carbon/TOU/EDF/equal-share baselines; it does not search routes.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Make carbon timing identifiable under dynamic arrivals and shared transformer limits.
candidates.complexity: Repeated finite-horizon optimization; grows with active vehicles, horizon slots, and shared constraints.
candidates.budget_accounting: Record every rolling optimization call and wall time; ALNS complete-solution budget remains separate.
failure_risks: US five-minute data do not match China thirty-minute inputs
candidates.minimum_isolated_probe: Clean-room formulation matched against equations and small analytical cases; no author-code import.

candidates.name: TOU_VNS_TS_WITH_CHARGING_REOPTIMIZATION
candidates.mechanism: Use cyclic exchange diversification plus 2-opt-star, exchange, relocate, and station insert/remove, and re-optimize charge timing after route changes.
candidates.formal_integration_point_if_approved: new ALNS neighborhoods calling the common charging oracle
candidates.difference_from_standard_alns: Couples route neighborhoods to time-of-use charging reoptimization instead of adding a generic local-search phase.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Improve exploration when route order changes charging-window and electricity-price opportunities.
candidates.complexity: Neighborhood size plus per-move charging subproblem cost.
candidates.budget_accounting: Each complete neighboring solution scored for selection consumes one evaluation; route-delta and charging-oracle calls remain visible.
failure_risks: oracle cost can starve route exploration
candidates.minimum_isolated_probe: Operator activity and non-duplication audit before any performance probe.

candidates.name: DEPOT_SHARED_CAPACITY_SCHEDULING_REFERENCE
candidates.mechanism: Schedule multiple EVs in fixed time slots under per-vehicle and hierarchical site power limits with time-of-use prices.
candidates.proposed_isolated_location: external archived reference or test fixture
candidates.formal_integration_point_if_approved: none preferred; independently implement a small common scheduling oracle
candidates.difference_from_standard_alns: Models depot charger/transformer contention explicitly; does not search routes.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Provide a reference for E5 shared charging capacity and baseline schedules.
candidates.complexity: Time slots multiplied by vehicles and infrastructure constraints.
candidates.budget_accounting: Reference calls and wall time are logged but do not silently alter ALNS evaluation count.
failure_risks: no nonlinear charging or carbon objective
candidates.minimum_isolated_probe: Read-only sample replay or independent formula cross-check after approval.

candidates.name: DUAL_ORACLE_CARBON_PRICE_CONFLICT_CHARGING
candidates.mechanism: Solve matched price-only and carbon-only fixed-route charging oracles, derive route-level conflict and slack scores, destroy high-conflict charging structures, and repair with a joint formal-objective oracle.
candidates.formal_integration_point_if_approved: dedicated carbon-price conflict destroy/repair operator and fixed-route charging oracle
candidates.difference_from_standard_alns: Uses disagreement between two matched charging oracles as a problem-specific destroy signal; not a parameter retune.
candidates.expected_benefit_hypothesis: Focus scarce evaluations on routes where time-varying price and carbon create actionable conflict while preserving nonlinear feasibility.
falsification_tests: operator activity must be nonzero on exposure-qualified cases
conflict ranking must outperform random charging-route selection under the same complete-evaluation budget
improvement must survive the carbon-blind paired control
wall-time cost must not eliminate route-search gains
candidates.complexity: Two diagnostic oracles per selected route plus one joint repair oracle; caching is essential.
candidates.budget_accounting: All oracle calls, cache hits, labels, generated complete candidates, accepted candidates, full evaluations, and wall time are separate counters.
failure_risks: conflict score may be redundant with time-window slack
multi-objective joint oracle semantics require approval
carbon benefit may remain small in total operational emissions
candidates.minimum_isolated_probe: Synthetic micro cases with known price-carbon agreement and conflict, followed by a result-blind China development subset only after approval.

arms.COST_ONLY_BLIND: reads time-of-use price and sets all slot carbon coefficients to zero
arms.CARBON_ONLY: reads carbon intensity and sets all slot electricity-price coefficients to zero
arms.JOINT_COST_CARBON: reads both signals under a separately approved formal objective

arms.CARBON_OPERATOR_OFF: carbon-guided conflict destroy and repair absent
arms.CARBON_OPERATOR_ON: carbon-guided conflict destroy and repair present

carbon_identification_contract.dynamic_e7_blind_arm: The carbon-blind arm must retain the same rolling mechanism, state inheritance, cooperation, fairness, nonlinear physics, price signal, oracle class, and budget; only future carbon information is hidden from scheduling and search guidance, while final settlement uses the same realized carbon profile.

excluded_as_algorithm_candidates.name: Carbon Aware SDK
excluded_as_algorithm_candidates.reason: Useful carbon-data API, not a vehicle-routing or charging-optimization algorithm.
